brief: A sturdy step for my toddler to stand on so they can reach the bathroom sink.

requirements.evidence: 4 full bases at level 0 plus 4 at level 1 (piece:0,0,0;full etc), 4 top covers (cover:0,0,1;full;top etc), ~364x467mm platform, 160mm tall, capOpenFaces + lockJoints applied, check_build ok meshClash clear
requirements.requirement: Sturdy low step platform for toddler to stand on

requirements.evidence: 2-storey height y=160mm gives lift toward sink; modest height suits toddler step
requirements.requirement: Enough height to reach bathroom sink

requirements.evidence: No tools verify grip, load rating, tip stability, or wet/slip safety; parts are 3D-printed in user-chosen material - adult supervision and non-slip placement needed
requirements.requirement: Safe for toddler use (non-slip, load-bearing, waterproof)

finish.summary: Built a 2-level, 4-cell platform (160mm tall) with solid top covers, capped faces and locked joints. check_build passes with mesh clear. Height helps reach sink but slip/load/wet safety cannot be verified here.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
